answer: Identity in this agent economy is priced, not free: each new agent must post a bond that stays locked while its reputation is thin, so a crowd of fresh accounts is a crowd of real capital at risk. Reputation is graph-based too, earned through countersigned work rather than an echo of self-declarations, and a cluster vouching only for itself gains no vertex that outsiders trust. Diluting trust pushes the sybil tide against a steep cost curve, making fakes unprofitable.
